title: Buyer growth — discovery language, one idea per ad

hierarchy: Advantage.Bid leads; one message; navy band closes
one event or message title of 2–6 words

merchandise.treatment: representative Advantage.Bid-owned items, visibly disclosed as representative — never presented as lots

typography.rule: one element may express contrast or material when truthful; brand faces only

transferable_lessons: 'Estate Sale' + 'Online Auction' stacked as a two-line event-type headline is an approved pattern for generic estate-auction creative
An exterior with staged merchandise is an acceptable environmental treatment for GENERIC estate creative (a real event uses its real photographs)
Category icon rows may name what buyers will find
Buyer growth = curiosity + discovery: 'finds', 'discover', 'unique', 'updates'; never seller language
A single red word inside a navy headline is an approved emphasis device
Email signup creative is a legitimate buyer-growth objective; the destination and form come from platform truth
Three icon rows (not four) suit buyer creative
A product screen may appear as a supporting prop inside a merchandise scene; it must never be the hero (rejected in 3P.1) and must show a real screen in production
'Join for Free' is acceptable only if buyer registration is free in production truth
Two-line contrast headlines suit buyer growth
Light foundation with a warm interior on one side is within the Owner's 'light' preference
A cardboard box as a 'your items' device is an approved narrative prop (representative, no claim)
Logo lockup at 40–50% of width is inside the Owner's comfort for Advantage.Bid-led creative (3P.1 set 30–40%; widen the ceiling to 50%)
The same concept may ship in two colour treatments within one campaign

brand_frame.band: navy Advantage.Bid band closes the canvas

principle_profile.structure_rule: name the structure chosen and why; consecutive creatives for the same objective rotate structure; a Gold is evidence, not a template

wording: Luxury finds for the discerning collector

omissions: product screen / laptop (a screen may be one supporting prop, never the hero — none used)
